div.head: Hu 2
div.ab: (Ðæt men faran on ryd æfter ðeofan.) Gyf neod on handa stande, cyðe hit man ðam hundredesmen, ⁊ he syððan ðam teoðingmannum; ⁊ faran ealle forð, ðær him God wisig[e], þæt hi tocuman moton; do ðam ðeofe his riht, swa hit ær Eadmundes cwide wæs.

Si necesse sit in manibus, indicetur hominibus hundredi, et ipsi postea indicent (denuntient) hominibus decimarum; et eant omnes pariter, quo Deus concedet (annuerit), ut inuenire possint; et faciant furi rectum suum, sicut prius Eadmundi regis fuit institutum.

Quodsi necessitas instet, primum nuncietur concionatori centenarii, qui deinde decimacionariis (id est singulis qui presunt decimacionibus); omnesque proficiscantur, quoadusque ducatu Dei perueniant quo cupiunt; furi quidem quod rectum est faciant, secundum quod ante ab Eadmundo rege institutum est.

Þæt men faran on cryd æfter ðeofan. Gyf neod on handa stande, cyðe hit man ðam hundredesmen, ⁊ he syððan ðam teoðingmannum; ⁊ faran ealle forð, ðær him God wisige, þæt hi tocuman moton; do ðam ðeofe his riht, swa hit ær Eadmundes cwide wæs.

(Dass die Männer hinter den Dieben im Zuge herjagen. B) Wenn dringende Noth vorhanden ist, künde man es dem Hundertvorsteher, und dieser dann den Zehntschaftvorstehern; und sie sollen alle hinausziehen, wohin ihnen Gott zeigt, dass sie zum [Ziel] kommen können; [man] vollziehe am Diebe dessen Rechts[strafe], wie es bisher (König Qu., Con.) Eadmunds Verordnung war.

(That the men pursue the thieves in a riding party. B) If there is urgent need, let it be announced to the hundred-man, and he then to the tithing-men; and they are all to go out wherever God shows them that they may reach [the goal]; [let] the thief's lawful [punishment] be carried out on him, as was previously (King, Qu., Con.) Edmund's ordinance.

That men go without delay in pursuit of thieves. If the need is urgent, the chief official of the hundred shall be informed, and shall forthwith inform the chief officials of the tithings, and all shall go forth, as God shall direct them, until they succeed in coming upon the thief. He shall receive his deserts as has already been decreed by Edmund.

If the need is urgent, one is to inform the man in charge of the hundred, and he then the men over the tithings; and all are to go forth, where God may guide them, that they may reach [the thief]. Justice is to be done on the thief as it was Edmund’s decree previously.

Die nicht archetype Überschrift deckt nur c. 2 und vielleicht 3. Sie bietet Mittelengl. Formen; ride für ‘Ritt’ kommt im 13. Jh. vor; Stratmann.—Childebert II. a. 596c. 9 (s. o. Einl. 6) befiehlt, jeder solle centenario ad malefactorem (prindendum) adiurare; ed. Boretius Mon. Germ., Capit. p. 17. Die Fränkische centena macht haftbar für dort Gestohlenes schon Chlothar c. 9, ebd. p. 5

The heading, which is not archetypal, covers only c. 2 and perhaps 3. It shows Middle English forms; ride for ‘riding’ occurs in the 13th cent.; Stratmann.—Childebert II. a. 596c. 9 (see above Introduction 6) orders that everyone should centenario ad malefactorem (prindendum) adiurare; ed. Boretius Mon. Germ., Capit. p. 17. Chlothar c. 9 already makes the Frankish centena liable for things stolen there, ibid. p. 5
Die Redensart (s. Wb: hand Z. 6 v. u. und Toller 508a) übersetzt Q zu silbenhaft
Q translates the idiom (see Wb: hand l. 6 from the bottom, and Toller 508a) too literally, syllable by syllable
Cons. meint mit concionator (s. Ducange) richtig den der Versammlung vorsitzenden Beamten. Dagegen verkennt Q den Dativ men als Plural (auch u. 5) und missversteht ‘Leute im Hundred’

By concionator (see Ducange) Cons. rightly means the official presiding over the assembly. Q, on the other hand, mistakes the dative men for a plural (also below 5) and misunderstands ‘people in the hundred’
Wiederum missversteht Q ‘Mitglieder der Zehnerschaft’; s. d. Gl 7—c.—Unglücklich erklärt den teoðingman als Sammler des Kirchenzehnten Morris Frankpledge 12
Again Q misunderstands ‘members of the tithing’; see that word in Gl 7—c.—Morris Frankpledge 12 unhappily explains the teoðingman as a collector of the church tithe
Gott (s. d. Gl 1) ist das Rechtsideal, das Volksgewissen; daher diese Wendung; sie meint nur dasselbe wie VI As 4
God (see that word in Gl 1) is the ideal of law, the conscience of the people; hence this phrase; it means only the same as VI As 4
to cuman ‘herankommen, ertappen’; s. Wb 212.—In VI As 8, 4 hatte was hier Amt des Hundertoberen ist der königliche Grafschaftsvogt verrichtet.—Vgl. Gl Gerüfte 1
to cuman ‘come up, catch’; see Wb 212.—In VI As 8, 4 what is here the office of the head of the hundred had been performed by the royal shire-reeve.—Cf. Gl Gerüfte 1

Archetyp las wie B do, ohne man. Denn Q übersetzt faciat, auch laut Hs. Rs.—Tod (III Em 2) samt Vermögenseinziehung ist gemeint. Denn zur Friedlosigkeit stimmt, dass Bestohlener nur einfachen Ersatz (s. d. Gl 1. 7) erhält: 2, 1

The archetype read do, like B, without man. For Q translates faciat, also according to MS Rs.—Death (III Em 2) together with confiscation of property is meant. For it is consistent with outlawry that the victim of the theft receives only single restitution (see that word in Gl 1. 7): 2, 1
cynges hatte laut Q Cons wahrscheinlich der Archetyp. Doch kann das Wort wie in VI As 11 gefehlt haben und von beiden Lateinern richtig ergänzt sein
According to Q Cons the archetype probably had cynges. But the word may have been lacking, as in VI As 11, and been correctly supplied by both Latin translators
The heading is found only in B.

Schmid and Liebermann read on ryd, the former adding a note ‘nicht ganz leserlich im MS.’ The writing is in faint red ink in the margin but the reading is clearly oncryd (without division). No such word occurs elsewhere but it would seem to be a legitimate abstract formation from crudan, similar to slege from slean or feng from fon. For the meaning compare Riddle, 4, l. 27 f. þonne hēah geþring / on cleofu crȳdeð and Sax. Chr. ann. 937 cread cnear on flot (Brunanburh, l. 35).

Lit. ‘the man of the hundred’ and ‘the men of the tithings,’ wrongly translated hominibus hundredi and hominibus decimarum (i.e. tithes) in Q.
The first mention of the tithing in the Laws occurs in VI As. 4, where it apparently refers to the groups of 10 men mentioned in the preceding clause. Such groups seem to have been organised for police purposes. By the time of Henry I the tithing had come to be regarded as a territorial division forming part of the hundred, cf. Hn. 6, 1 b. Regarding the history of the tithing see further Liebermann, ii, s.v. Zehnerschaft; Stubbs, Const. Hist. i. pp. 91–6; P. and M. i. pp. 568–71.
Cf. II As. 2, 1; VI As. 6, 3.
There is no extant law of Edmund’s which does state definitely what is to be done with the thief, although it is clear enough from VI As. 1.
